name: Train your Marines as a team
definition: Every waking hour Marines should be trained and schooled, challenged and tested, and corrected and encouraged with perfection and teamwork as a goal.

terms.label: train your Marines as a team

rows.situation: When the next hard week is coming
rows.under: Lets each person practice alone and hopes they will join up under pressure.
rows.justRight: Practices the real handoffs as a group, with the same load they will carry.
rows.over: Schedules so much group practice that nobody can finish this week's work.

rows.situation: When someone is new to the team
rows.under: Leaves them to discover their seat by colliding with someone else's.
rows.justRight: Makes the role, the handoff, and who they back up explicit, then practices it.
rows.over: Writes a role chart so detailed that they cannot move when the plan breaks.

rows.situation: When the group is a set of specialists
rows.under: Staffs the seats and treats a team as something that appears later.
rows.justRight: Trains, works, and reviews as a group, so each person knows how their piece serves the others.
rows.over: Blends every role so thoroughly that nobody is accountable for a piece.

rows.situation: When practice could be easy or real
rows.under: Runs a rehearsal that never stresses the weak join.
rows.justRight: Makes the practice hard enough that the real day is familiar, and corrects without humiliation.
rows.over: Turns practice into punishment, and people hide the misses you needed to see.

rows.under: Picks one person to blame and leaves the join-up unfixed.
rows.justRight: Names the handoff that failed, practices that piece, and keeps the people in their seats.
rows.over: Makes every miss a full reset of the team, and nobody trusts the next practice.
